newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Premium seen in Brazil Cemig auction.
newsitem.headline: Premium seen in Brazil Cemig auction.

text.p: BNDESpar, the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), expects to auction debentures in Minas Gerais state power firm Cemig for more than the minimum price, a BNDESpar official said.

BNDESpar is auctioning 18.7 million debentures, convertible into a 32.9 percent voting stake in Cemig, April 25 on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange for 60.37 reais ($56.95) per debenture to a strategic partner.
"Financing and payment facilities were designed in such a way to boost the chances of a premium during the auction," said BNDESpar Director Durval Soledade.
He said BNDES would finance up to 500 million reais ($471.7 million) of the final auction price paid for the debentures, be the buyer a Brazilian or foreign company.

The buyer will have to pay in cash 50 percent of the minimum price as well as any premium achieved during the auction by April 30. The remaining 50 percent of the minimum price can be paid with two promissory notes redeemable within one year after the auction, Soledade said.

One note worth 10 percent of the 50 percent will be payable to BNDESpar and the other worth 90 percent of the 50 percent will be payable to the Minas Gerais state government, which has a 60 percent stake in Cemig.
The debentures were issued to BNDESPar in exchange for BNDES loans granted to Cemig for new investments, amounting to around 550 million reais, including interest accrued.
Soledade said the proceeds from the auction would be used to pay off the Cemig loans and the rest would be divided between BNDESpar and the Minas Gerais state government.
BNDESpar will receive 10 percent of the remaining receipts and Minas Gerais state 90 percent.
Minas Gerais Finance Secretary Joao Heraldo Lima said the funds would be used for development projects in areas such as education and irrigation.
He said a number of companies including French Electricite de France, U.S. Southern Co and Chile's Chilectra SA had shown interest in Cemig.

Under the sell-off rules, only a single company is allowed to acquire the Cemig debentures and no consortia will be admitted to the auction. However, a group of firms can create a company for the purpose of the auction.
Interested investors have to prequalify for the auction by March 31.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
